topic: What if you could pause time, but only while you hold your breath?
title: WHAT IF YOU COULD
PAUSE TIME?

script.text: You drop your phone. Pause. Catch it. Play.
A paper ball flies at your face. Pause. Step aside. Play.
Your best friend, mid-laugh. Pause. Not even blinking.

script.beat: 2 the premise and its rule (title card)
script.text: What if you could pause time, but only while you hold your breath?

script.beat: 4 the turn: the cost, one real fact
script.text: Most people last about a minute. The world record, on pure oxygen, is twenty-nine minutes. That's real.
So how long can you hold yours?

science.claim: Most people can hold their breath for about a minute.
science.working: Clinical and science sources put an untrained healthy adult at about 30 to 90 seconds; 'about a minute' is the middle of that range, and Outside notes most people struggle to reach one minute without practice.
science.source: Acibadem (most healthy adults 30-90 s); BBC Science Focus (no longer than 90 s); Outside Online

science.claim: The world record, on pure oxygen, is twenty-nine minutes.
science.working: Vitomir Maričić, 29 min 03.07 s, Opatija, Croatia, 14 June 2025, Guinness 'Longest time breath held voluntarily underwater (male)', oxygen-assisted (pure oxygen breathed beforehand). It beat Budimir Šobat's 24:37 (2021). 29:03 rounds to 'twenty-nine minutes'.
science.source: Guinness World Records, longest-time-breath-held-voluntarily-male; Guinness news, Sept 2025
